title: Talon agent-switch re-entry card on Sidecar: phase 1 (route to macbook-ops secondmate, fixer)
description:
ROUTE TO: the macbook-ops secondmate (the captain calls it "fixer"). It owns Sidecar (local-only Go repo at fm_home/macbook-ops/projects/sidecar). Do not route to displayd (older Python daemon) and do not clone Sidecar into any other home.

FILED 2026-10-24 by the mini0-ops firstmate on the captain's instruction. The captain is still planning the rest with mini0-ops; further decisions arrive as comments on this bead. Phase 1 below is cleared to begin.

THE CAPTAIN'S WORDS (verbatim, voice-dictated):
"I have my MacBook as my development environment right now. I'm using Talonvoice through it and I am running into problems of recollection of where I am, which is hard for me. Basically, it's easy for me to lose focus for what's exactly going on because I'm trying to work on many things at once, but I have just implemented the recall system to change windows. So I'm saying words like mayor, fixer, zephyr, often, which are the names of programming windows. ... it would be really great if in my talon setup that actually emitted an event that the sidecar stream could process to show me information about what I've been trying to do in that particular agent window given what I have said."
Then: "Dispatch an agent to begin on the first part" and "make sure to note that it should go to the second mate ops one, which is fixer".

PROBLEM (evaluation): not forgetting; each voice switch lands him in an agent window with no goal cue, so he re-reads to rebuild context. Each switch is the right moment to show a re-entry card.

THE SYSTEM, NEEDED REGARDLESS: (1) a switch trigger: Talon fires when an alias is spoken (agent, time, spoken alias); (2) a last-seen record per agent plus what he last said to it; (3) turning agent activity into facts (deterministic extraction; see data/turn-summarizer-deterministic/report.md on mini0, recommends fields not sentences, ~1 ms, never invents identifiers); (4) alias to agent mapping that survives restarts (herdr tab/pane ids change; plugin/recall/herdr_focus.py already resolves by agent name or cwd); (5) fast (about 1 s), non-blocking, fail-silent, local-only (transcripts hold secrets, show fields only); (6) some surface that shows it.
PREFERENCE, NOT NEEDED: where it shows (Sidecar, terminal overlay, phone, spoken aloud via Kokoro), exact fields and density, Sidecar event-stream column, LLM polish (measured not worth it), "while you were away" alerts, history, per-task grouping, an on-demand "where am I" voice command (nearly free; consider it).

PHASE 1 (begin here; no Sidecar code changes): in the Talon recall plugin (trillium_talon/plugin/recall/herdr_focus.py, action herdr_focus_tab), after the focus succeeds, fire an async non-blocking step that builds a small re-entry card for that agent and puts it on a Sidecar pane with the existing POST /v1/show (docs/show.md, docs/api.md; local markdown or HTML file). Card fields, fixed and short: (a) what he last asked this agent; (b) what it did since; (c) its state: working, waiting on him, or blocked; (d) what changed since he last looked. Inputs: Talon utterance history for that agent, the agent's session transcript tail and status files, herdr agent state. Sidecar invariant must hold: the device reports its viewport, Sidecar owns layout, the card never scrolls, so keep it small. The switch command must never be delayed or broken by this; any failure is silent.
PHASE 2 (not yet): proper event emission and a Sidecar stream column, plus "since you left" deltas. Needs a Sidecar generic event-ingest route; the README says the stream server side still lives in displayd, so confirm what exists first.

FIRST QUESTIONS FOR THE OWNER: who owns the Talon repo (trillium_talon); what does "what I have said" cover (voice commands only, or typed text too: the captain has not answered; default to voice commands and say so); what does the macbook-ops backlog already hold on Sidecar.
GUARDRAILS: Sidecar is local-only: never push, no remote. Never print or store transcript text beyond what the card needs; keep it on the MacBook. Conventional commits, no tags.

title: Build First Mate Urgency Protocol  -  interactive captain-facing execution agent
description:
# First Mate Urgency Protocol  -  Captain's request

## Problem and purpose
I needed six separate print-ready QR-code PDFs, each with a unique code, for a time-sensitive in-person marketing event. An agent made a tear-off sheet instead, and First Mate's brief-writing and asynchronous delegation consumed the time available for correction. I left the event without the materials. The underlying friction is that First Mate's normal delegation process is too slow for immediate tasks. This is a process problem, not merely a prompt-clarity problem.

## Architecture
First Mate recognizes an immediate task and promptly launches a temporary, captain-facing interactive Urgency Agent, passing the relevant context and bounded authority. The Urgency Agent is a powerful hands-on worker, not a second First Mate or another orchestration layer. I converse directly with it, clarify requirements, inspect deliverables, and request corrections in real time. First Mate stays out of the critical execution path after launch. Normal delegation remains available for nonurgent tasks.

## Native sub-agent authorization
The Urgency Agent's initial configuration EXPLICITLY PREAUTHORIZES use of native sub-agents. In Claude Code it may invoke Claude Code's built-in sub-agents; in Pi it may use its enabled native/installed sub-agent mechanism, and similarly in other runtimes. It must not create First Mate delegation briefs, launch separate First Mate-managed workers for internal subtasks, or follow the normal First Mate delegation/reporting cycle. It operates within its authorized scope and native runtime guardrails; actions outside the grant require my direct authorization.

## Lifecycle
The agent works in an accessible interactive window until I explicitly declare the task complete, or a configurable inactivity timeout occurs (ten hours was a suggestion, not a finalized requirement). Preserve outputs and useful context before cleanup. Avoid repetitive checks for already-authorized actions.

## Desired result
I can request immediate execution, get a capable interactive worker promptly, use preauthorized native sub-agents, iterate directly, and receive correct artifacts before my real-world deadline. The feature is only accepted after I, the captain, approve the actual workflow.

## Verification tests
1. Immediate launch: request urgent work; verify direct access to an interactive agent without a background briefing queue; measure time to session.
2. Claude Code: verify native sub-agent execution within its session, without First Mate briefs.
3. Pi: with native/installed sub-agents enabled, verify analogous execution without First Mate delegation.
4. Permissions: verify in-scope actions proceed without repeated approvals and out-of-scope actions request my direct authorization.
5. QR regression: generate six separate print-ready PDFs with six distinct QR codes; inspect uniqueness, scan destinations, layout, and interactive corrections.
6. Latency: compare time to session, first usable artifact, correction, and accepted completion against standard delegation; agree on thresholds with me.
7. Lifecycle: test explicit completion, output retention, configurable idle timeout, cleanup and recovery.
8. Fallback: if native sub-agents or interactive windows are unavailable, report that immediately rather than silently reverting to slow delegation.
9. Captain signoff: I verify a realistic urgent task meets my deadline and approve the result.

## Open design questions
Urgency detection versus explicit invocation; runtime selection; authority transfer; interactive window mechanics; capability discovery; timeout and resumption; output preservation; failure handling. Prototype the core workflow without waiting for every question to be settled.

## Definition of done
I can reliably launch an interactive urgency worker, direct it live, use preauthorized native sub-agents, receive correct time-sensitive deliverables, close the session, and explicitly sign off as captain.

title: Create Research Store for Voice and Language Model Training
description: Request for the agent handling this bead: create a dedicated research knowledge store to collect, organize, and retrieve research documentation, academic papers, white papers, and technical references on speech recognition, dictation, voice model training, large language model training, and related machine-learning methods. Establish a clear structure for sources, citations, summaries, topics, and ongoing additions so this becomes a durable research library supporting Open Speech Model Development (project-he8k). Include research on distributed/federated training and user-contributed compute as an initial topic, but the store must cover the broader research domain. This bead requests creation of the research store, not execution of the research itself.

Design a simple accessible share extension UI with clear destination selection and sensible defaults; support offline/error handling, authentication, deduplication, and retry without duplicate submissions. Clarify whether 'brain stones' means brain stores/Beads stores; use existing architecture rather than inventing a new backend. title: Build MVP of Standalone Parrot-Enabled Web Browser
description: Captain explicitly requests a working MVP now, not just research/design. First Mate: deduplicate against any existing implementation task before dispatch; if one already exists, adopt and prioritize it rather than build twice. Related inbox-1j44 (standalone browser, NOT Safari extension), inbox-3kt1 (shared voice/sound platform), and completed design scout brain-fmhscout-voice-sound-platform-design-q1. Build a usable standalone browser with Parrot sound recognition integrated, using the captain's existing trained Parrot model where technically feasible without retraining or repeated downloads. Core MVP: load and navigate real webpages; microphone permission and listening on/off; detect configured lip pops/clicks; map them to scroll/page up/down with adjustable bindings; visible recognition feedback; simple setup and diagnostic screen; graceful failures. Favor the fastest viable platform from the design scout and explicitly document platform selection, model format/runtime, latency, security (do not load untrusted pickle), constraints, and any unsupported reuse path. Prioritize a working end-to-end vertical slice over broad platform infrastructure or Rango/grammar expansion. Acceptance tests: browse several real pages, verify pop/click scroll in both directions, configure mappings, reuse existing model, show false positives/latency, repeat after restart; document build/run steps and remaining gaps. Report actual working demo, tests, and blockers to this bead. Coordinate with project-xvzw and existing Parrot projects; create project implementation child as appropriate.

title: Research Shared Voice and Sound Interactions Across iOS Apps
description: Urgent research request: determine how independently developed iPhone/iOS applications can share voice commands, user-defined grammar, sound-recognition models, and standardized navigation actions. Explore a reusable library of Talon Hub community-compatible interactions (next, previous, select, back, etc.) that participating apps can adopt, reusing speech/sound models already available on the phone rather than redownloading or retraining them. Investigate feasible iOS mechanisms and restrictions for model sharing, app-to-app interoperability, shared settings/grammars, SDKs, app groups, extensions, background execution, accessibility APIs, and navigation within versus between apps. Explicitly distinguish realistic in-app navigation from unsupported system-wide control. Compare architecture options, security/privacy constraints, and developer integration effort. Recommend the smallest practical proof of concept, tests, and a go/no-go conclusion with primary-source Apple documentation and relevant Talon/Parrot references. Coordinate with shared platform concept inbox-3kt1 and browser concept inbox-1j44; avoid duplicating their scope.

title: Shared Voice and Sound Control Platform Across Applications
description: Explore a reusable platform for voice and sound interaction across connected applications, including iPhone apps and a web browser. Provide shared user-defined voice grammar and vocabulary so custom command choices carry across apps (e.g., user says 'Risk' for letter R instead of 'Red'). Support Rango-style selection of on-screen links and controls, potentially with labeled/numbered targets, and investigate a configurable grammar as a platform-level capability. Integrate reusable/composable Parrot sound recognition and user-trained models so applications can share sound triggers without repeated training or model downloads. The standalone Parrot-enabled browser concept is captured in inbox-1j44; explicitly connect and coordinate that browser bead as an early consumer/proof of concept of this platform. Investigate shared configuration, interoperability, accessibility, and platform constraints before deciding implementation.

title: Safari Sound-Controlled Page Navigation with Composable Parrot Model
description: Explore and implement a Safari browser application or extension that lets users navigate pages hands-free using configurable mouth sounds, such as pops and clicks mapped to Page Up and Page Down. The sound-recognition model must be composable: users should be able to reuse an existing Parrot/chaosparrot.py-compatible personal sound model rather than retraining or downloading a duplicate model for every application. Investigate the feasible Safari integration surface, how to load or connect a user's model, map recognized sound events to browser scrolling/navigation actions, and expose simple configurable bindings. Keep the scope focused on a working Safari proof of concept and document compatibility constraints and acceptance tests. Related to Open Speech Model Development / Voice-Native Gaming (project-he8k.1), but captured as an inbox request for triage.

title: Make tldraw-deck slide screenshot previews a durable, repeatable workflow
description: Extend the existing tldraw-deck slide screenshot effort (inbox-af2d, tldraw-slide-shots, project-fmh-tldraw-deck). Do not treat screenshots as a one-time deliverable. Build and document a durable, repeatable command/script/workflow in the tldraw-deck repository that can be run on demand whenever slides, layouts, live panels, or presentation configuration change. It should start or connect to the real presentation, enumerate every slide from slides.config.json in current order, navigate to each intended camera framing in presentation mode, wait for animations/render and live-panel readiness with explicit timeout/error reporting, capture one clearly named screenshot per slide, and regenerate an easy-to-browse indexed gallery/contact sheet with slide number, title, capture timestamp, and live/mock/error status. Make output paths predictable, avoid stale screenshots, and preserve snapshots when desired. Include exact one-command usage, dependencies, setup, cleanup, security/redaction for sensitive live data, reproducibility and smoke tests, and a clear way to inspect artifacts from ChatGPT or another accessible location. Verify by running the workflow and reporting the resulting artifacts. Coordinate with the in-progress scout and link its output; avoid duplicate implementations. Ensure this remains useful after future slide additions/reorders/edits.

title: Create private GitHub remote for tldraw-deck and capture screenshots of every planned presentation slide

Do not make the repository public or expose secrets, tokens, private event data, or local-only files; inspect gitignore and tracked content before pushing. Then run the actual tldraw spatial presentation MVP and capture an individual screenshot for EVERY currently configured slide in slides.config.json, in presentation mode at its intended camera framing, in the existing order. Include slide number, title, screenshot path, and brief explanation of visible content; distinguish real/live data from placeholders or unavailable integrations. Provide an easily browsable index/contact sheet or gallery plus individual screenshots, with accessible artifact locations and clear instructions for reviewing them. If a remote cannot be created because of missing authorization, report the precise blocker and next action. If screenshots cannot be captured, report exact blockers and do not substitute imagined visuals. Attach completion evidence and links/paths to this inbox bead and durable Brain report. Coordinate with existing tldraw-deck work and preserve the MVP.
